physicalNotes: Radius 0.34079816 Jupiter radii from Morello et al. 2026 (2026MNRAS.549ag183M), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026MNRAS.549ag183M/abstract): 24,364.3 km at 71,492 km per Jupiter radius. GM from the mass 0.044 Jupiter masses (the NASA Exoplanet Archive's calculated value (M-R relationship, its Chen & Kipping 2017 mass-radius relationship): a model, not a measurement, via the NASA Exoplanet Archive, https://exoplanetarchive.ipac.caltech.edu/docs/pscp_calc.html) times JPL's Jupiter GM. A sphere: no oblateness is measured.

sources.period: Morello et al. 2026 (2026MNRAS.549ag183M), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname MORELLO_ET_AL_2026): P 2.260424 d
sources.shape: Morello et al. 2026 (2026MNRAS.549ag183M), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname MORELLO_ET_AL_2026): a/R* 9.32; Morello et al. 2026 (2026MNRAS.549ag183M), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname MORELLO_ET_AL_2026): inclination 88.85 degrees
sources.eccentricity: No archive row states an eccentricity; the orbit is taken as circular
sources.phase: Morello et al. 2026 (2026MNRAS.549ag183M), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname MORELLO_ET_AL_2026): transit mid-time 2459820.1815 BJD, taken as BJD_TDB; with its period, the row that predicts 2026-01-01 best (1 sigma 3 min)
sources.orientation: Display convention: transit photometry does not measure the orbit's position angle on the sky, so the ascending node is set at position angle 0 (celestial north).
